question: 请依据 Microsoft FY2025 10-K，提供 Microsoft Cloud、Intelligent Cloud 与 Azure 的口径定义及 FY2025 对应披露指标，明确金额/增长率差异，不推算未披露Azure收入。

facts.rationale: This block gives the original definition of the Microsoft Cloud metric and its components. The table is indivisible, so it also carries the unrequested commercial RPO and gross margin rows.

citations.quote: Revenue from Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, Azure and other cloud services, the commercial portion of LinkedIn, and Dynamics 365

facts.rationale: This is the list introduction. It sets the FY2025 vs FY2024 comparison period for the 23% and 34% growth figures.

citations.quote: Highlights from fiscal year 2025 compared with fiscal year 2024 included:

facts.rationale: This block states the disclosed FY2025 Microsoft Cloud revenue amount and growth rate.

citations.quote: Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9 billion.

facts.rationale: Section heading that establishes which segment the definition list belongs to.

citations.quote: Intelligent Cloud

facts.rationale: This block defines the Intelligent Cloud segment scope. It also introduces the enumeration with the qualifier 'primarily comprises'.

citations.quote: Our Intelligent Cloud segment consists of our public, private, and hybrid server products and cloud services that power modern business and developers. This segment primarily comprises:

facts.rationale: This is the first enumerated item of Intelligent Cloud. It defines the composition of Azure and other cloud services and places that line within server products and cloud services.

citations.quote: Azure and other cloud services, comprising cloud and AI consumption-based services, GitHub cloud services, Nuance Healthcare cloud services, virtual desktop offerings, and other cloud services

facts.rationale: This is the second and final enumerated item of Intelligent Cloud. The reading group shows all item bodies delivered, so the segment enumeration is complete.

citations.quote: Enterprise and partner services, including Enterprise Support Services, Industry Solutions, Nuance professional services, Microsoft Partner Network, and Learning Experience.

facts.rationale: The segment table gives Intelligent Cloud FY2025 revenue and operating income in millions, with FY2024 comparatives and growth rates. The other segment rows sit in the same indivisible table.

citations.quote: (In millions, except percentages) 2025 2024 PercentageChange
Intelligent Cloud Revenue $ 106,265 $ 87,464 21%
Operating Income $ 44,589 $ 37,813 18%

facts.rationale: This block gives the disclosed Azure and other cloud services growth (34%) and its parent line's growth (23%). It contains no dollar amount for Azure.

citations.quote: Server products and cloud services revenue increased 23% driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.

requirements.rationale:
Both the definition and the FY2025 metric are delivered:
- The definition lists four components, including Azure and other cloud services, showing Microsoft Cloud is a cross-segment company metric rather than a segment.
- The FY2025 amount ($168.9B) and growth (23%) are given against FY2024.

citations.quote: Revenue from Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud, Azure and other cloud services, the commercial portion of LinkedIn, and Dynamics 365
Microsoft Cloud revenue increased 23% to $168.9 billion.
Highlights from fiscal year 2025 compared with fiscal year 2024 included:

requirements.rationale: The segment definition and both enumerated items are delivered; only bullet markers are undelivered. FY2025 segment revenue and operating income are given in millions, with FY2024 comparatives and growth rates.

citations.quote: This segment primarily comprises:
Enterprise and partner services
Intelligent Cloud Revenue $ 106,265 $ 87,464 21%

requirements.rationale:
Two parts are supported:
- The composition and affiliation of Azure and other cloud services.
- Its FY2025 growth rate of 34%.

The question, however, requires a clear statement of the amount-versus-growth difference and that no undisclosed Azure revenue is estimated. That needs evidence on whether the 10-K discloses an Azure dollar amount anywhere. Under query_evidence_v1 only selected blocks are delivered. The delivered text cannot establish non-disclosure. The revenue-by-product disaggregation note and the Intelligent Cloud segment MD&A discussion, where such an amount or the parent server products and cloud services amount would appear, were not delivered.

citations.quote: Server products and cloud services, including Azure and other cloud services
driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.

source_checks.rationale: The delivered text has no image or chart gaps. It supports all three definitions, the Microsoft Cloud and Intelligent Cloud amounts, and Azure growth. It is selected evidence only, though. It does not show whether the 10-K discloses an Azure (or Azure and other cloud services) dollar amount, or what amount the parent server products and cloud services line shows. The revenue disaggregation by product/service and the Intelligent Cloud segment results discussion are needed to support the 'amount not disclosed' distinction.

citations.quote: Server products and cloud services revenue increased 23% driven by Azure and other cloud services revenue growth of 34%.

assessment.coverage_reason:
Two of the three concepts are fully covered:
- Microsoft Cloud: definition, FY2025 amount and growth.
- Intelligent Cloud: full definition enumeration, FY2025 revenue and operating income with growth.

Azure's definition and 34% growth are supported. The question's amount-versus-growth distinction, including that no Azure revenue amount is disclosed, cannot be confirmed from the selected blocks. The 10-K sections where an Azure or parent-line amount would be disclosed were not delivered.
missing_information: 10-K revenue disaggregation by significant product and service offerings (FY2025 vs FY2024). This shows the server products and cloud services amount and whether any Azure / Azure and other cloud services dollar amount is disclosed.
10-K Intelligent Cloud segment results discussion in MD&A. This confirms whether Azure is disclosed only as a growth rate, with no standalone revenue amount.

body_checks.rationale: Short segment heading that anchors the affiliation of the definition list.
Intelligent Cloud segment definition and list introduction with its 'primarily comprises' qualifier.
First segment item; defines Azure and other cloud services and its placement within server products and cloud services.
Second segment item, needed to complete the Intelligent Cloud enumeration.
List introduction that establishes the FY2025 vs FY2024 period for the highlight growth rates.
FY2025 Microsoft Cloud revenue amount and growth.
Azure and other cloud services growth and parent line growth; this is the only Azure metric delivered.
Contains the Microsoft Cloud metric definition. The extra rows are part of the same indivisible table.
Intelligent Cloud revenue and operating income with units and comparatives. Other segment rows are part of the same indivisible table.

limitations: Block 561 is an indivisible table that also contains the unrequested commercial RPO and Microsoft Cloud gross margin rows; retained because the Microsoft Cloud definition row is necessary.

Block 587 is an indivisible segment table that also contains the Productivity and Business Processes, More Personal Computing and Total rows; retained because the Intelligent Cloud rows and the units header are necessary.
Units differ: Microsoft Cloud is stated in billions in MD&A highlights, while the segment table is in millions. The answer should keep these units distinct.
Microsoft Cloud and Intelligent Cloud overlap but are different scopes: a company-wide metric versus a reporting segment. Their amounts should not be compared or netted to derive Azure revenue.
